findings.source_quote: πᾶσιν δίδου· πᾶσιν γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς δίδοσθαι θέλει ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων δωρημάτων.
findings.english_quote: Give to all[j], for God wants all to be given from his own gifts[o].
findings.issue: In the explanatory clause, πᾶσιν denotes the recipients: God wants giving to reach everyone. “All to be given” instead makes “all” the subject of the passive infinitive, suggesting everything is to be given, or that everyone is themselves to be given. This loses the repeated recipient wording and introduces an unsupported object or scope of giving. Footnote o compounds the defect by claiming that this wording retains “all” without adding an object or amount; it does not accurately represent the dative construction.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “Give to all, for God wants everyone to receive from his own gifts.” Alternatively, retain the passive explicitly: “Give to all, for God wants gifts from his own gifts to be given to everyone.” Revise footnote o to explain that both occurrences of πᾶσιν identify recipients, while retaining its bounded disclosure about God/Lord and the reported preposition readings.

findings.source_quote: πᾶσιν δίδου· πᾶσιν γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς δίδοσθαι θέλει ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων δωρημάτων.
findings.english_quote: Give to all[j], for God wants all to be given from his own gifts[o].
findings.issue: Independently against the Greek, the simplified explanatory clause fails to express πᾶσιν as the recipients of giving. “All to be given” makes “all” sound like what is given, rather than those to whom giving is directed. The preceding imperative does not repair this clause-level change. The shared footnote o incorrectly endorses the wording as preserving the source without supplying an object or amount.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “Give to everyone, because God wants everyone to receive from his own gifts.” Update footnote o to identify the repeated recipient expression and preserve the reported textual alternatives without changing the selected reading.

summary: Both editions were reviewed separately against all seven selected Greek paragraphs. Both require correction of the recipient construction in II.4 and its explanatory note. Otherwise, the conditional liability, repeated prohibitions and giving instructions, explicit non-judgment of afflicted recipients, giver’s innocence, life promise, and household repentance are retained. Contextual repentance follows current policy; no δοῦλος occurrence requires a servant rendering here. The notes disclose the reported heart conjecture, additional bracketed pronoun, witness differences, and restoration limits without requiring replacement of the selected working readings. This is a model review of the supplied text and attributed evidence reports, not authentication of unseen editions, images, handwriting, or exhaustive collation. Proposed replacements remain subject to fresh review.
